title: Not Just Any Example: Security Requirements and Fix Patterns for Guiding LLM Vulnerability Repair
abstract: arXiv:2611.31993v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Software vulnerabilities leave systems open to attack, and their remediation is often delayed. Large language models (LLMs) have advanced automated patch generation, yet passing functionality tests does not ensure that a patch enforces the security requirement the vulnerability violated. Existing vulnerability repair techniques rely on curated patterns or templates with limited coverage, leaving unclear which repair strategies carry over across vulnerabilities and how they can steer LLMs. We present a large-scale empirical study that relates recurring fix patterns to the security impacts of vulnerabilities and examines how this knowledge can guide LLM-based repair. Building on a manual study of security patches, we cluster 3,816 security patches from 348 open-source repositories and analyze the edits and their context to derive concrete fix patterns, ranging from local safeguards to coordinated changes across multiple locations. translated_title: 并非任意示例：用于指导大语言模型漏洞修复的安全需求与修复模式
translated_abstract: 软件漏洞使系统面临攻击风险，而漏洞的修复往往被延误。大语言模型（LLM）在自动化补丁生成方面取得了进展，然而通过功能性测试并不意味着补丁能够满足漏洞所违反的安全需求。现有的漏洞修复技术依赖于人工整理的、覆盖范围有限的模式或模板，因此尚不清楚哪些修复策略可以跨漏洞通用，以及如何利用这些策略来引导大语言模型。我们提出了一项大规模实证研究，将重复出现的修复模式与漏洞的安全影响相关联，并考察这些知识如何指导基于大语言模型的修复。在对安全补丁进行人工研究的基础上，我们对来自348个开源代码仓库的3,816个安全补丁进行了聚类，并分析代码修改及其上下文，以推导出具体的修复模式，涵盖从局部防护措施到跨多个位置的协同修改等多种类型。
tldr: 该论文通过对348个开源仓库中3,816个安全补丁的大规模实证研究，提炼出与漏洞安全影响相关联的具体修复模式，并展示了如何利用这些模式引导大语言模型生成真正满足安全需求的漏洞修复补丁。
en_tdlr: Through a large-scale empirical study of 3,816 security patches from 348 open-source repositories, this paper derives concrete fix patterns linked to vulnerabilities' security impacts and shows how this knowledge can guide LLMs to generate patches that actually enforce security requirements.
